body:
# Setups page: two orientation dropdowns (plane + point), same section everywhere

## What

The setup alignment UI is scattered across five separate sections
(preset/angles picker, lay-on-plane row, lay-on-points row, part-axes
rows, work-offset label). Collapse it into ONE section with TWO
dropdowns, drawn identically wherever a setup's orientation is edited:

- **Plane orientation** - how the part's frame is set:
  `Axes` (the two-pick 3D alignment, #769), `Points` (the three-point
  lay, #555), `Face` (the face lay, #330), `Cylinder angle` (NEW: two
  curved-face picks give a bore/cylinder axis; it lands on a chosen
  world axis, turned by an angle about it), `Manual` (the preset combo
  and typed angles, #326/#606).
- **Orientation point** - where the setup's WCS origin sits:
  `From model box` (the parts' bounds - corner or centre), `From stock
  box` (the setup's stock bounds - corner or centre), `Manual point`
  (pick a vertex in the viewport). Placing the point keeps the WCS's
  rotation: the frame comes from the plane dropdown, the point only
  moves the origin.

Selecting an entry expands its controls below the dropdown. Existing
functions are reused verbatim as the expanded content; the completing
work is the cylinder-angle backend and the per-setup origin placement.

## Everywhere the same

The section is one component mounted in BOTH places that edit a
setup's orientation: the Setups overview (every setup stacked) and each
setup's own Settings page. Same dropdowns, same options, same look.

## Done means

- Both pages show the same two dropdowns; picking an option expands
  exactly that option's controls; the old flows still work through
  them (the row functions keep their own entry points, so their
  existing tests stay green untouched).
- `Cylinder angle`: two curved-face picks on a bore land its axis on
  the chosen world axis with the typed angle about it; refusals by
  name (same face twice, coincident centroids, non-finite).
- The orientation point places the named setup's WCS origin (corner /
  centre of the model or stock box, or a picked vertex), rotation kept;
  undo restores. Inactive setups place their own WCS, not the active
  one's.
- UI tests: the section expands, both mount points draw it, the origin
  lands per setup.
